messages.body_plain:
Thank Kirill and Joe.

 It seems that to create a separate html manual file is indeed the least painful, but the html file cannot include any iframe, otherwise, it can not be displayed in Shiny. So I have to write  the manual in html, including a lot of math formulas. It's not easy to edit the file.

Using Google drive is another good way, it can even show the doc file in Shiny, however, the file must be set to public accessible. If the manual is confidential and private, this method doesn't work.

For some reason,  tags$iframe(src="manual.pdf", width="900", height="600")  doesn't work in my Shiny. I use Firefox.

I think frame and iframe functions need to be improved in Shiny.

Zhilan

messages.subject: Re: input type="Password" does not work by default
messages.subject_clean: input type="Password" does not work by default
messages.body_plain:
Hi Michael,

General steps I believe can be found in many online resources (I am sure you can find some good videos on youtube); the only exposure to this topic that I had is back when I worked with ASP.NET <http://ASP.NET> 2.0... and many things came out of the box. I think one of the approaches you can consider is to start with designing the GUI for your Shiny page(s). It will help you to have a list of functionality (or functions) that you would need to code. It may be something simple, just a log in page for a couple of users,

or it can be more complex that includes sign in/registration form, password reset/recovery etc. In latter case you'd probably need a number of separate pages and as far

as I understand that would mean running several Shiny sites (Shiny server). After GUI part is done, you can move on to the database side, if you need to.

Again, in some complex scenario, you'd probably need some repository to keep users names/passwords/temp user's session tokens etc. Then it is easier to write up your functions related to authenticating a user and keeping the track of some sort of session token. You can assign a token to the user's session and then pass it over from one page to another by using a URL parameter and then read it by using intrinsic Shiny's session object: shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {}).

I don't think you need JavaScript to implement this functionality. R + Shiny framework should be enough for that. If you need all this for some sort of enterprise/commercial application, you might check on the current offers from RStudio folks. I have not been following them for a month or so, unfortunately, but they were planning to release some commercial server that supposedly includes authentication capabilities as well. Hope this helps.

> Timur and Ramnath,Thank you so much for posting such clear steps for others like me to follow. I really appreciate it!
>
> Timur, if I may ask, what were general steps that you took in creating your own authentication? I saw some users attempting to do the same and I am interested in giving it a shot myself -- however my Javascript experience right now is next to none.
>
> Thanks again,

> > > >
> > > >
> > > > On Mon, Jul 22, 2013 at 3:31 PM, Timur Medjitov <tmedz...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > Okay, I finally made it work.
> > > > > The solution is basically based on what Ramnath originally suggested.
> > > > > I have patched my local copy of the shiny.js with input binding for type = password.
> > > > >
> > > > >  Steps are:
> > > > >
> > > > > 1. Make a local copy of shiny.js --> shiny_copy.js
> > > > > On my machine it is located in the installation folder of the shiny package: C:\Users\mtimur\R\win-library\3.0\shiny\www\shared
> > > > >
> > > > > 2. Open shiny.js in a text editor
> > > > >
> > > > > 3. Find the section for "// Text input" and insert this snippet of code (the key point here is: 'input[type="password" )
> > > > >
> > > > > // Password input
> > > > >
> > > > > var passwordInputBinding = new InputBinding();
> > > > > $.extend(passwordInputBinding, {
> > > > >   find: function(scope) {
> > > > >     return $(scope).find('input[type="password"]');
> > > > >   },
> > > > >   getId: function(el) {
> > > > >     return InputBinding.prototype.getId.call(this, el) || el.name <http://el.name>;
> > > > >   },
> > > > >   getValue: function(el) {
> > > > >     return el.value;
> > > > >   },
> > > > >   setValue: function(el, value) {
> > > > >     el.value = value;
> > > > >   },
> > > > >   subscribe: function(el, callback) {
> > > > >     $(el).on('keyup.passwordInputBinding input.passwordInputBinding', function(event) {
> > > > >       callback(true);
> > > > >     });
> > > > >     $(el).on('change.passwordInputBinding', function(event) {
> > > > >       callback(false);
> > > > >     });
> > > > >   },
> > > > >   unsubscribe: function(el) {
> > > > >     $(el).off('.passwordInputBinding');
> > > > >   },
> > > > >   receiveMessage: function(el, data) {
> > > > >     if (data.hasOwnProperty('value'))
> > > > >       this.setValue(el, data.value);
> > > > >
> > > > >     if (data.hasOwnProperty('label'))
> > > > >       $(el).parent().find('label[for=' + el.id <http://el.id> + ']').text(data.label);
> > > > >
> > > > >     $(el).trigger('change');
> > > > >   },
> > > > >   getState: function(el) {
> > > > >     return {
> > > > >       label: $(el).parent().find('label[for=' + el.id <http://el.id> + ']').text(),
> > > > >       value: el.value
> > > > >     };
> > > > >   },
> > > > >   getRatePolicy: function() {
> > > > >     return {
> > > > >       policy: 'debounce',
> > > > >       delay: 250
> > > > >     };
> > > > >   }
> > > > > });
> > > > > inputBindings.register(passwordInputBinding, 'shiny.textInput');
> > > > >
> > > > > // end of block
> > > > >
> > > > > 4. Save the file.
> > > > >
> > > > > Another option is to save this code in a file xxx.js in your projects' www directory and call it from ui.R or server.R by using
> > > > > tags$script(src = 'xxx.js'), but it will give you 'file not found' error. (you can see the error in the browser's debugger:
> > > > > ctrl+shift+I in Chrome)
> > > > > I even tried to save it in www/js directory as it was suggested in one of the threads here  - same error.
> > > > > So, patching the shiny.js as outlined above works fine.
> > > > >
> > > > > Thanks.
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > On Sunday, July 21, 2013 5:18:50 AM UTC-4, Ramnath Vaidyanathan wrote:
> > > > > > > You can save the JS as custombindings.js in a folder named www (it is important that the folder be named www), and then in ui.R, call it using
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > tags$script(src = 'custombindings.js')
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Let me know if this works.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > On Saturday, July 20, 2013 11:05:04 PM UTC-4, Timur M wrote:
> > > > > > > > Hi Alex,
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > Did you find a solution to this problem? I am also stuck with this and I am not sure the JS
> > > > > > > > code provided by Ramnath can be used directly in ui.R.

> > > > > > > > Timur

messages.subject: Input & Output components suggestion
messages.body_plain:
As I use Shiny more I think there should be a new type of component that is an input as well as an output. Currently some input components have update methods and of course we can use renderUI to achieve this effect. But I think it's better to have a a natural class components that can act as both input and output.

I am building an app where the output is a table. The user can dynamically change the component table and I would like to read the table as input and make further adjustments. Specifically the app can build a model using say logistic regression and the user can replace variables in the front end and refit the model using the updated list of variables.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny server restricted access?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I believe that using the combination .htaccess and .htpasswd files should be working (I did not try it myself).
I succeeded in a similar way using nginx instead of Apache to get things lighter and using the htpasswd files. The customer accesses its own area with login and password and then can browse through its own shiny apps.
I also added an SSL layer (HTTPS) to make things secured. Let me know if you need more details (I guess it would be too long to explain it on a forum).

JB

Le vendredi 23 août 2013 09:23:37 UTC+2, Thibault Helleputte a écrit :
> No I didn't succeed that way.
>
> Finally, I think the best way in the long run is to play with session variables. Which I didn't tried out yet.
>
> For the moment I opted for a temporary solution: a text field and two buttons: "lock" and "unlock". A passphrase is defined on the server side. This key must be entered in the text field and "unlock" sends the value to the server. If the key is correct, all the rest of the application is made visible to the user.
>
> Now the trick is that, if you define the rest of the application -which is supposed to be protected- on the client side within a simple conditionalPanel(), your protection will be very poor: the supposedly protected content is merely "hidden" by javascript/css, but still accessible from the source code of the page. So you have to define all the protected content on the server side, and use a renderUI() on server side, coupled with a uiOutput() on client side.
>
> Finally, almost everything is defined on server side, and almost nothing on the client side, except for the lock/unlock panel.
>
>

messages.subject_clean: Interactive 3D WebGL in Shiny via RGL
messages.body_plain:
I've been working on a more formal integration of RGL (Interactive 3D WebGL in R) and Shiny in a "shinyRGL" package.

http://trestletech.github.io/shinyRGL/ (with an interactive demo)
https://github.com/trestletech/shinyRGL (code and installation instructions)

After installing the package, you can run the two Shiny apps in the 'inst/examples' directory to get a feel for what's possible. I have a patch outstanding with the 'rgl' package that will enable a couple of nice usability features -- hopefully that patch will be accepted shortly. shinyRGL package is backward-compatible with the version of rgl that's on CRAN now, however.

Any feedback is welcome! Code is available under MIT license.

messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to display a word or pdf file in a panel?
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to display a word or pdf file in a panel?
messages.body_plain:
On Sun, Sep 1, 2013 at 3:36 PM, Zhilan Ming <zhil...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Thank Kirill and Joe.
>
>  It seems that to create a separate html manual file is indeed the least painful, but the html file cannot include any iframe, otherwise, it can not be displayed in Shiny. So I have to write  the manual in html, including a lot of math formulas. It's not easy to edit the file.
>
> Using Google drive is another good way, it can even show the doc file in Shiny, however, the file must be set to public accessible. If the manual is confidential and private, this method doesn't work.
>
> For some reason,  tags$iframe(src="manual.pdf", width="900", height="600")  doesn't work in my Shiny. I use Firefox.
>
> I think frame and iframe functions need to be improved in Shiny.
>

The iframe function in Shiny just outputs HTML, so there's nothing really that can be changed about it:
> tags$iframe(src = "foo.pdf")
[1] "<iframe src=\"foo.pdf\"></iframe>"
attr(,"html")
[1] TRUE

As for displaying PDFs in an iframe, it works fine for me using Chrome, although not all browsers will be able to do it. Did you put your file manual.pdf in a www/ subdirectory? Just like when you write an index.html file by hand, you need to put in www/. See: http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#html-ui

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Excel in a Shiny app
messages.body_plain:
Data processing is done with R; you can do whatever you want, e.g. you
can read any files as long as you can find a package/function to do it
(read.csv() for CSV files, packages for Excel files to read Excel
files, ...). This part is orthogonal to Shiny.

What Shiny can do for you is to provide a user interface to upload the
files in the beginning (or other UI elements to provide input
options), and display results using the UI elements in the end.
Everything else in the middle depends on the power of R and you have
full freedom (in other words, that part is basically a general R
problem). I hope this is clearer now.

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.subject: Re: spark server usage limitations?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jim,

I like your apps! Thanks for your consideration regarding performance.

We currently have Spark configured to allow 200 concurrent users on each application before we'll start showing the "Server Overloaded" message. (This was a fairly recent change to Spark, however, so you may have found different performance patterns previously.) That being said, the user experience offered on most apps with 200 concurrent users won't be very pleasant; remember that R is single-threaded, so any time R is doing computation for one user, the other 199 would have be waiting.

They grayed out screen should be a rare byproduct of one of us doing work on the server -- we try to minimize that as much as possible. Are you seeing that more than, say, once a day?

All in all, if your application is computationally light enough to fluidly support 30 (or 50, or 100) simultaneous users, then you shouldn't find Spark to be limiting!

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: ERROR: cannot open the connection
messages.body_plain:
With Shiny Server, you should put the apps in a directory like /home/username/ShinyApps/myapp  (In the instructions, the ~ stands for /home/username.)
Then you should be able to visit it with a web browser at:
http://spark.rstudio.com/username/myapp/

runApp() is really only for local development, and it won't work properly on Glimmer and Spark.

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: conditional panel based on renderPlot output?
messages.subject_clean: conditional panel based on renderPlot output?
messages.body_plain:
SOLUTION:

The condition I was setting condition = "output.histPlot" tests if the histPlot output container has internal content.  In the case of plots, this would be an img tag.  However, when an app is launched, there is blank (white) placeholder img in place, thus the condition returns TRUE.

To get around this, I added the following to my ui.R:

> uiOutput('plotDone')

and the following to my server.R:

> output$histPlot = renderPlot({
>   output$plotDone <<- renderUI({tags$input(type="hidden", value="TRUE")})

>   ... plot code ...
> })

I can now set the condition for my conditional panel as:

> conditionalPanel(condition = "output.plotDone", downloadButton(...), ...)

Lee

messages.subject: Re: conditional panel based on renderPlot output?
messages.subject_clean: conditional panel based on renderPlot output?
messages.body_plain:
Wouldn't it have been simpler to have the conditional panel dependent on clicking an action button which was simultaneously holding back the renderPlot from execution?

On Wednesday, September 4, 2013 11:52:54 AM UTC-4, Lee Pang wrote:
> SOLUTION:
>
> The condition I was setting condition = "output.histPlot" tests if the histPlot output container has internal content.  In the case of plots, this would be an img tag.  However, when an app is launched, there is blank (white) placeholder img in place, thus the condition returns TRUE.
>
> To get around this, I added the following to my ui.R:
>
> > uiOutput('plotDone')
>
> and the following to my server.R:
>
> > output$histPlot = renderPlot({
> >   output$plotDone <<- renderUI({tags$input(type="hidden", value="TRUE")})
> >   ... plot code ...
> > })
>
> I can now set the condition for my conditional panel as:
>
> > conditionalPanel(condition = "output.plotDone", downloadButton(...), ...)
>
> Lee
>
> On Wednesday, September 4, 2013 8:27:27 AM UTC-7, Lee Pang wrote:
> > Hi All,
> >
> > I have an app where I would like to display a download button only if a plot has been rendered.
> >
> > I've placed the button in a conditional panel like so:
> >
> > > conditionalPanel(condition = "output.histPlot", downloadButton(...), ...)
> >
> > where histPlot is produced by:
> >
> > > output$histPlot = renderPlot({ ... plot code ... })
> >
> > When I run my app, the button is displayed when the plot is not - basically ignoring the condition.
> > Am I missing something here?
> >
> > Thanks,
> > Lee
messages.body_snippet:
Wouldn't it have been simpler to have the conditional panel dependent on clicking an action button which was simultaneously holding back the renderPlot from execution?

messages.subject: Re: chart context menu?
messages.body_plain:
A follow-up to partially answer my own question, the bootstrap framework is included in every shiny app (I didn't know that before) so it simply a matter of invoking the right incantations in bootstrap to get a button with a dropdown menu.

In the sidebarPanel in ui.R I now have,

>             ## bootstrap dropdown menu code shamelessly stolen from
>             ## http://stackoverflow.com/a/13998987/1135316
>             ##
>             div(class="dropdown btn-group",
>                 a(img(src="navicon.svg"), class="btn dropdown-toggle", "data-toggle"="dropdown", href="#",
>                   span(class="caret")),
>                 tags$ul(class="dropdown-menu",
>                         tags$li(a("Foo", href="#", target="_blank")),
>                         tags$li(a("Bar", href="#", target="_blank")))),

This gives me the button and dropdown menu I was looking for.  Now to position it over the chart and hook up the menu to shiny actions.
>

Or use updateSelectInput (probably the preferred approach these days).

In your server function (since we need the "session" object, make sure your Shiny server function has the signature function(input, output, session) ):

observe({
  if (is.null(input$file1))
    return()
  dat <- read.csv(inFile$datapath, header = T)
  updateSelectInput(session, "cols", choices = names(dat))
})

#ui.R
library(shiny)

# Define UI for random distribution application
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
# Application title
headerPanel("Tabsets"),
# Sidebar with controls to select the random distribution type
# and number of observations to generate. Note the use of the br()
# element to introduce extra vertical spacing
sidebarPanel(
radioButtons("dist", "Distribution type:",
list("Normal" = "norm",
"Uniform" = "unif",
"Log-normal" = "lnorm",
"Exponential" = "exp")),
br(),
sliderInput("n",
"Number of observations:",
value = 500,
min = 1,
max = 1000)
),
# Show a tabset that includes a plot, summary, and table view
# of the generated distribution
mainPanel(
tabsetPanel(
tabPanel("Plot", plotOutput("plot"),div(id="linkToSummary",tags$a("This is a link to Summary Tab")) ),
tabPanel("Summary", verbatimTextOutput("summary")),
tabPanel("Table", tableOutput("table"),HTML("<script>$('#linkToSummary').click(function() {
tabs = $('.tabbable .nav.nav-tabs li')
tabs.each(function() {
$(this).removeClass('active')
})
$(tabs[1]).addClass('active')
tabsContents = $('.tabbable .tab-content .tab-pane')
tabsContents.each(function() {
$(this).removeClass('active')
})
$(tabsContents[1]).addClass('active')

$('#summary').trigger('change')

})</script>
") )
)
)
))

#server.R

library(shiny)

# Define server logic for random distribution application
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
# Reactive expression to generate the requested distribution. This is
# called whenever the inputs change. The renderers defined
# below then all use the value computed from this expression
data <- reactive({
dist <- switch(input$dist,
  norm = rnorm,
  unif = runif,
  lnorm = rlnorm,
  exp = rexp,
  rnorm)
dist(input$n)
})
# Generate a plot of the data. Also uses the inputs to build the
# plot label. Note that the dependencies on both the inputs and
# the 'data' reactive expression are both tracked, and all expressions
# are called in the sequence implied by the dependency graph
output$plot <- renderPlot({
dist <- input$dist
n <- input$n
hist(data(),
main=paste('r', dist, '(', n, ')', sep=''))
})
# Generate a summary of the data
output$summary <- renderPrint({
summary(data())
})
# Generate an HTML table view of the data
output$table <- renderTable({
data.frame(x=data())
})
})

messages.subject: Re: Shiny, two process the same time.
messages.subject_clean: Shiny, two process the same time.
messages.body_plain:
The two clients shouldn't receive the same result, unless you are doing something weird with global state. However, it would still be desirable to have two processes because the R process can only do work for one client at a time. The ability to have multiple processes per app will be a feature of the upcoming commercial version of Shiny Server. It is not available in the Open Source version.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Best practice to (re)use RJDBC / SQL server connections in Shiny app
messages.subject_clean: Best practice to (re)use RJDBC / SQL server connections in Shiny app
messages.body_plain:
My experience with RDBMS is all from the Java world, not R, but in general I don't think it's a good idea to use a connection across multiple users, whether single-threaded or not. Transaction scope is tied to a connection so you really only want to use a connection for the lifetime of something you could consider a logical transaction.

Performance-wise you would want your DB driver or framework to implement connection pooling for you, so opening "new connection" from your code would not be too expensive. However I don't know if RJDBC implements connection pooling or not--I see no evidence of this. Still, I'd start with relatively short-lived, isolated connections until you see that there is a performance/scalability problem.

Hello Folks!

I've been wondering recently if it's possible to use Phonegap (http://phonegap.com/), to package a Shiny app into a little  for use on iOS, Android etc.

As far as I understand Phonegap, it's basically just a wrapper around something which launches a web page in the native browser. It also has some additional features for notifications, etc.

I haven't done any work on it yet, but I was just wondering if anyone else had had a go, or if they know of any technical reasons why it might be problematic or a bad idea.

Best,

Brendan

Hi all,

I have built an Shiny app on my VPS and I can see my app from http://my_site.com:3838

If I want to see the app from  http://my_site.com , How should I redirect the URL?

I read the Shiny Server Configuration Reference, and using the redirect{} in a wrong way.

Could anybody help my to fix the problem?

-------------------------
Here is my Shiny-server.conf

run_as shiny;

server {
  listen 3838;

  location / {
    site_dir /var/www/html/my_site/public_html;
    log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;
    directory_index on;
  }

redirect "my_site.net <http://my_site.net>";  <====That's wrong

}

-----------------------------
Here is my vhost.conf

NameVirtualHost bbb.bbb.bbb.bbb:80
<VirtualHost bbb.bbb.bbb.bbb:80>
     DocumentRoot /var/www/html/forbidden
     ServerName bbb.bbb.bbb.bbb
</VirtualHost>

<VirtualHost bbb.bbb.bbb.bbb:80>

     CustomLog /var/www/html/my_site.net/logs/access.log <http://my_site.net/logs/access.log> combined
</VirtualHost>

Regards,
Jack

messages.subject: looking for some paid help to refine my Shiny App
messages.subject_clean: looking for some paid help to refine my Shiny App
messages.body_plain:
Shiny App Community,

I have put together a relatively simple Shiny App that I need some help refining.  99% of the app works, but I need some help making a couple improvements.

App Description:
My app is a data checking and submission app that has a sidebar and main panel. The sidebar has three tabs that do the following:
Tab #1 - Allows the user to upload their data in a CSV format
Tab #2 - Allows the user to fix their data by specifying appropriate data ranges and certain quick-fix type operations
Tab #3 - Allows the user to submit their data to me
The main panel is also tabbed and shows a summary of the data errors some individual tables that show specific error types.

Help Needed:
What I need help with is putting the final touches on this thing ...
Implement the "Submit" button that either emails me the data or places it somewhere on a server for me to pick up,
Implement a data loading / progress button -- I expect some of the CSV files to be in the range of 30mb and I want the user to see progress on the operation,
Small visual changes -- e.g. the tabs in the sidebar are white instead of grey ... guessing this can probably be done with CSS, and
Generally look over the web app and provide recommendations for performance improvements

Payment: USD 50-75 per hour (Elance.com, PayPal or similar)

Start date: Immediately

messages.subject: Re: Caching of Objects
messages.body_plain:
Whether an object is "cached" across all sessions or not is determined by which scope you use when loading it:
http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#scoping

You can get the best of both worlds by using the new reactiveFileReader function, and calling it above the server function. This way, it'll be visible across all sessions, but it'll automatically update itself when the file changes on disk, and trigger reactive expressions and observers/outputs that depend on it.

address 0x12ec57f8, cause 'memory not mapped'

 ggplot2(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg)) + geom_point()

Then, if the problem still happens, remove a piece of code above, and repeat until the problem disappears. This should help to diagnose the problem.

I have two questions about this:

messages.subject: Re: Slow processing time for subsetting in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: Slow processing time for subsetting in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
You should probably avoid the subset() function, because it uses non-standard evaluation of its arguments. From ?subset:
"This is a convenience function intended for use interactively. For programming it is better to use the standard subsetting functions like [, and in particular the non-standard evaluation of argument subset can have unanticipated consequences."

That said, the use of subset() instead of [ is probably not the source of the performance problem. There are a number of other things that happen in Shiny - for example, if you're sending a big table from the server to the browser, it needs to be converted to JSON and sent over the network.

If you put those print(Sys.time()) lines directly around the subset() call in your shiny app (and monitor the printed output at the R console), what's the time difference?

-Winston

Thanks again for everyones help, the solution is below :)

The reactivity daisy chaining was working all along, the issue was with the "Round" column being loaded as a factor, and factors persist as a dataframe attribute after subsetting. Thus I needed to use droplevels() after subsetting the data. I added dat <- droplevels(dat) below:

  # Second data load (filter by service column)
  serviceFiltered_clientData <- reactive({
    dat <- clientData()
    if (is.null(dat))
      return(NULL)
    if (!is.null(input$service_select)) # !
      dat <- dat[dat$Service.Name %in% input$service_select,]

    dat <- droplevels(dat) # This is what fixed it
    return(dat)
  })

On Mon, Sep 9, 2013 at 1:12 PM, <rohan...@gmail.com> wrote:

>
> Hi,
>
> I am totally new to Shiny. I want to use it for association rule mining. I couln't find any example of Shiny regarding association rule mining. I created a small data set and I ran association rule mining on it. I only want to show all the generated rules on the browser but I have problem to do that.
> I have attached dataset txt file. And here is the code to generate the rules:
>
> After importing the dataset in R you should do:
>
> library(arules)
> #changing data  type to factor
> for(i in 1:10){
> dataset[,i]<-factor(dataset[,i])
> }
> #generating rules
> rules<-apriori(dataset,parameter=list(support=0.20,confidence=0.20,minlen=2))
> #displaying rules

Hi,

I'm trying to change the color of some rows in a renderTable output -- but it seems like the arguments sent to print.xtable are just being printed as text at the top of the table. Clearly I'm doing something wrong! Below is a slightly modified shiny tutorial example (the add.to.row line in server.R)...

thanks,
Tracy

server.R
-----------
library(shiny)
library(datasets)

# Define server logic required to summarize and view the selected dataset
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # Return the requested dataset
  datasetInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$dataset,
           "rock" = rock,
           "pressure" = pressure,
           "cars" = cars)
  })

  # Generate a summary of the dataset
  output$summary <- renderPrint({
    dataset <- datasetInput()
    summary(dataset)
  })

  # Show the first "n" observations
  output$view <- renderTable({
    head(datasetInput(), n = input$obs)
  }, add.to.row = list(pos = as.list(1:3), command = rep("\\rowcolor[gray]{.8} ", 3)))
})

-------

    numericInput("obs", "Number of observations to view:", 10)

messages.body_plain:
Hi Winston,

Very Interesting. We should chat more.

We tried switching to rjson in rCharts and it lead to a huge performance gain. However, rjson only works with some of the JS libraries in rCharts, as the others require more elaborate data structures, which are provided only by RJSONIO.

Maybe, there is a strong use case now to either enhance rjson to provide the same functionality as RJSONIO, or improve RJSONIO to match the speed of rjson.

Alternately, there might be some fast C++ libraries that can be wrapped using Rcpp.

I would be happy to discuss more.

Cheers,
R

messages.subject: Re: shiny-server cannot find the non-standard R library
messages.subject_clean: shiny-server cannot find the non-standard R library
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sean,

I think the issue is which user has these libraries installed. If you open R and run `.libPaths()`, you'll be able to see which paths are included in your library search paths. These will likely be different for different users.

Now the question is which set of .libPaths is shiny-server using, and that will depend on how you have it configured. If you're using the autouser configuration, then each user's library will be used, because the applications will be run as that user. If you're using site_dir or app_dir, then the `run_as` setting will dictate which user runs Shiny (thus which .libPaths will be used).

My guess is that the `run_as` user you're using doesn't have these libraries installed. If that's the case, log in as that user, open R, and install the libraries.

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: Caching of Objects
messages.body_plain:
You would use rm(), the same as removing any other objects from any other environment in R. However, like any other R script, if there are references to these objects being maintained in the sessions, those don't automatically disappear (it would be really confusing if they did--like dangling pointers <http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangling_pointer> in C).

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server URL
messages.body_plain:
(Thanks for bringing the question over here, Taylor).

We'd recommend using Shiny Server for any real hosting of Shiny Apps. Shiny by itself would be a bit of a headache to manage (you'd have to spin up R and maintain R processes for each Shiny application you want to host, map them to particular ports, etc.) Shiny Server handles all that for you so you can have a single daemon process on the server that hosts all of these applications for you (and offers a variety of other perks as seen on the README of the GitHub project).

Regarding the URL, I apologize that we don't have this formally documented publicly just yet. However, we're just finishing up the first draft of some documentation internally, and I can post the relevant section to you here. The short answer is: pick a port on which you want Shiny Server to run then you can setup your URLs be prefaced by whatever you want. Documentation is copied below (sorry if the formatting gets weird in email. If it's unreadable, let me know and I can generate a PDF).

Jeff

Server Hierarchy

Detailed descriptions of all available parameters are available in the appendix, but it is important to understand the overall hierarchy of the Shiny Server configuration file when editing the file.
Server

The server setting defines an HTTP server which will listen on a port/IP address combination. For example, the following lines:
server {
  listen 80;
}

define a server that would listen on port 80. A server can also define a server_name to limit the virtual hostnames on which it listens, as described in the Virtual Hosts section.
Location

The location setting is defined within a server and defines how a particular URL path should be served. For instance, the following settings:
server {
  ...
  # Define the location '/specialApp'
  location /specialApp {
    # Run this location in 'app_dir' mode, which will host a single Shiny
    # Application available at '/srv/shiny-server/myApp'
    app_dir /srv/shiny-server/myApp
  }

  # Define the location '/otherApps'
  location /otherApps {
    # Run this location in 'site_dir' mode, which hosts the entire directory
    # tree at '/srv/shiny-server/apps'
    site_dir /srv/shiny-server/apps;
  }
...
}

would define two locations, one which serves (potentially) a multitude of applications at the URL /otherApps/, and another which serves a single application at the URL /specialApp/.

The various hosting models which can be applied to a location are described in the section on Hosting Models.
Application

The application block is specified within a location and defines the settings related to a particular application. The application is referenced by the directory in which it is stored. For example, the following configuration could be used to modify the application housed at /srv/shiny-server/app1.
...
location / {
  # Define rules to apply to one application, stored at '/srv/shiny-server/app1'
  application /srv/shiny-server/app1 {
    simple_scheduler;
  }
}
...

This block would specify that, within this location, the referenced application should use the Simple Scheduler. This setting would have no effect on the other applications hosted in this location block.

Hosting Model

There are currently four different methods of configuring a location, three of which serve Shiny applications. These three are described below; see the following section on Redirecting to learn about a fourth mode.
app_dir

A location configured to use app_dir will attempt to serve a single application hosted at the given directory. For instance,
# Define the location '/specialApp'
location /specialApp {
  app_dir /srv/shiny-server/myApp;
}

will configure the location responsible for the path /specialApp to use this app_dir router which serves a single application stored in the directory /srv/shiny-server/myApp. This configuration would presume a server.R file (and corresponding ui.R file) would be available at /srv/shiny-server/myApp/server.R.
site_dir

A location which uses site_dir will host an entire directory tree -- both Shiny Apps and static assets.
# Define the location '/'
location / {
  site_dir /srv/shiny-server/
}

The above configuration would instruct Shiny Server to make the /srv/shiny-server/ directory available at the base URL. Any Shiny applications stored in this directory (or any subdirectory), along with any static assets (including images, data, JavaScript/CSS files, etc.) will be made available at the corresponding URL. For example, see the following directory tree:
+---/srv/shiny-server
|   +---shinyApp1
|       +---server.R
|       +---ui.R
|   +---shinyApp2
|       +---server.R
|       +---ui.R
|   +---assets
|       +---style.css
|       +---script.js

If this server were available at http://server.com, the location settings above would make the following (along with any other file in the tree) publicly available to the user.

http://server.com/shinyApp1

Serve the Shiny App defined in 'shinyApp1'

http://server.com/shinyApp2

Serve the Shiny App defined in 'shinyApp2'

http://server.com/assets/style.css

Serve this static CSS file

http://server.com/assets/script.js

Serve this static JS file
user_apps

A location configured to use user_apps will allow users on the system to create and manage their own Shiny applications available in their home directories. This directive will host any application stored in an eligible user's ~/ShinyApps directory publicly at a URL prefaced by their username.

This privilege can be restricted only to users of particular groups using the members_of restriction. For instance, the following configuration:
# Define the location '/userApps'
location /userApps {
  user_apps;

  # Only allow members of the 'shinyUsers' group to host personal applications.
  members_of shinyUsers;

messages.body_plain:
If you can mix and match them using HTML + JavaScript, then you should be able to mix and match them using shinyUI as well. In the particular case of our pageWithSidebar and gridster, since each of those has a pretty strong opinion about what the overall layout of the page is like, you might have trouble there. But for other things like Google Charts, JustGage, d3, etc. the components generally play nice on the same page. One key thing to remember is that everything inside of the shinyUI call, is merely a producer of HTML. Take any sub-expression of shinyUI and print it at the console and you'll see what it does. If you have two components that don't work together, try printing (or use cat(as.character(...)) for nicer looking output) each of them out and see if you can figure out why they are not compatible. server.R:
```
mytabsetPanel <- function (tabs, id = NULL, selected = NULL)
{
  #tabs <- list(...)
  tabNavList <- tags$ul(class = "nav nav-tabs", id = id)
  tabContent <- tags$div(class = "tab-content")
  firstTab <- TRUE
  tabsetId <- as.integer(stats::runif(1, 1, 10000))
  tabId <- 1
  for (divTag in tabs) {
    thisId <- paste("tab", tabsetId, tabId, sep = "-")
    divTag$attribs$id <- thisId
    tabId <- tabId + 1
    tabValue <- divTag$attribs$`data-value`
    if (!is.null(tabValue) && is.null(id)) {
      stop("tabsetPanel doesn't have an id assigned, but one of its tabPanels ",
           "has a value. The value won't be sent without an id.")
    }
    liTag <- tags$li(tags$a(href = paste("#", thisId, sep = ""),
                            `data-toggle` = "tab", `data-value` = tabValue, divTag$attribs$title))
    if (is.null(tabValue)) {
      tabValue <- divTag$attribs$title
    }
    if ((firstTab && is.null(selected)) || (!is.null(selected) &&
                                              identical(selected, tabValue))) {
      liTag$attribs$class <- "active"
      divTag$attribs$class <- "tab-pane active"
      firstTab = FALSE
    }
    divTag$attribs$title <- NULL
    tabNavList <- tagAppendChild(tabNavList, liTag)
    tabContent <- tagAppendChild(tabContent, divTag)
  }
  tabDiv <- tags$div(class = "tabbable", tabNavList, tabContent)
}

messages.subject: Re: Generating a series of tabPanels
messages.body_plain:
If the only difference between mytabsetPanel and Shiny's own tabsetPanel is that the former takes a list of tabs as an argument instead of the individual tabs, then you could also accomplish that by calling tabsetPanel using do.call:

tabs <- ...
tabs$id <- 'tab0'
do.call(tabsetPanel, tabs)

This is not very intuitive, perhaps we should just change tabsetPanel to accept either list or ... tabsetPanels. (Come to think of it, that is how tabPanel and all the other panels work.)

Other than your MetaDynamicUI5 code looks like a sensible approach to me--I'm glad you were able to figure this out (and sorry for not weighing in sooner). Although I do wonder if rather than having the four separate reactive expressions under "preliminary objects", it would be more convenient to have a single reactive that does all of those calculations at the same time and returns them as a dataframe/list? Performance-wise it should be about the same because they all have the same dependencies--though if in your real application they have different dependencies then by all means keep them separate.

require(shinyGridster); can also be placed outside of shinyUI like so

require(shinyGridster);

Not really, the normal idiom is just to call library(shinyGridster) at the top of ui.R. Your way works equally well but is harder to read and it's also nice to be able to look at the top of the file to see what libraries are depended on.

> Is it documented, or more in general is there a sequence diagram somewhere that would help me understand object interaction/timelines so I don't ask too many dumb questions?

Not really, if you're asking how ui.R and server.R are loaded and how shinyUI/shinyServer are implemented. If you haven't read the scoping <http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#scoping> chapter of the tutorial, that may help.

> Open question: are folks using shinyGridster, am I barking up the wrong tree? I like it and want it...

The package was developed by one of the Shiny maintainers and will likely become "official" at some point in the future, so as far as non-Shiny-core components go, it's a pretty safe bet.

> Can I get a grey (or indeed gray) backgound so my white background grid panes can be visually cued as 'objects' or 'panes'?

Yes, you can just use CSS for that. Include this somewhere in your shinyUI (replace #888888 with whatever shade of grey <http://www.colorpicker.com/> you want):

tags$style(type="text/css", "body { background-color: #888888; }")

> Apart from that and referring to shiny itself, I get intermittent 'shockwave crashed :(' problems googleVis which crash the object, not shiny, especially when I click the 'line plot' tab, so I'm kind of giving up on googleVis for now... not your problem, I know, but maybe some other users have comments or workarounds.

You could try my bindings <https://github.com/jcheng5/googleCharts>, they use a different approach to integrate googleVis with Shiny that should be more robust if these crashes have to do with reactivity causing the plots to be updated. (At some point in the future you'll see these bindings integrated into the googleVis package proper, once I have a little more time.)

> I use an animated slider instead, which works but but it has a couple of UE issues: (1) fine locally, but clunky remotely for any multi-pane graphics (OK, I know, it's asking a lot - but that's where googleVis excels with it's interpolation/anti-aliasing) (2) Can't seem to control the speed other than changing the 'step' argument on the slider.

I'm not clear on what you mean by #1. For #2, see ?animationOptions; you can use this instead of TRUE when passing the animate argument to sliderInput. One of the options it lets you set is the interval.

>
> This is all fine-tuning, really.
>
> Oh, did I say, what a cool thing is shiny?!  Life-enhancing.

Thanks :)

>
> Giles

))

             div(class='span4', numericInput(lwr, "Lower limit", value=NA)),
             div(class='span4', numericInput(upr, "Upper limit", value=NA))
))

Error in as.character(x) :

tags$div(class='row-fluid',
         div(class='span4', numericInput(lwr, "Lower limit", value=NA)),
         div(class='span4', numericInput(upr, "Upper limit", value=NA))
)
```

messages.subject: Re: Performance, parallelism
messages.body_plain:
Hello, Alex.  I have been trying for days to work around this problem. We are developing an app that requires a lengthy calculation to run. While it is running, it locks out all other users from accessing the site. Unfortunately, implementing a solution similar to your multicore (using parallel (i.e., mcparallel, mccollect)) does not seem to fix our problem. Were you ultimately successful?

Thanks in advance!
Shannon

On Wednesday, March 6, 2013 5:38:46 PM UTC-5, Alex wrote:
> The multicore::parallel seems to be working nice with Shiny, with additional advantage of giving live feedback from worker process.
> A simple example of implementation:
>
> 1) Simulate expensive function:
>
> f <- function(x) {
> for(i in 1:3) {
> multicore::sendMaster(as.character(i))
> Sys.sleep(2)
> }
> sqrt(x)
> }
> 2) Run in server:
>
> values <- reactiveValues( res=NULL, calcMsg1 = NULL )
> observe( {
> if (is.null(proc)) {
> proc <<- multicore::parallel(f( 10 )))
> values$calcMsg1 <- 'Started'
> invalidateLater(1000)
> } else if ( multicore::selectChildren(proc) == multicore::processID(proc) ) {
> res <- multicore::collect(proc, wait=FALSE)[[1]]
> if( class(res) == 'character' ) {
> invalidateLater(1000)
> values$calcMsg1 <- res
> } else {
> multicore::collect(proc)
> proc <<- NULL
> values$res <- res
> values$calcMsg1 <-  paste('FINISHED:',res)
> }
> } else { invalidateLater(1000); }
> }, label='CalcMain', suspended = FALSE )
>
> After execution we have final result in values$res.
> While execution we can send feedback to browser using values$calcMsg1.
>
> Notes:
>
> proc = NULL was initially defied inside shinyServer function parameters, e.g. shinyServer(function(input, output, proc = NULL) { ...
> This allows different browser connections fork multiple workers, while only 1 worker is allowed per connection. I believe it can be also defined as reactive value.
>
> Last multicore::collect(proc) is mainly to ensure that R cleaned-up after forking and we would not run into memory problems.
>
> I advise to use multicore::children() to limit number of workers depending on number of cores and available memory.
>
> The function assumes that message class is 'character' and final result class is NOT 'character'. This can be easily fixed by defining and returning e.g. "message" class object.
>
> Joe, you are right that this would not work for all apps, but in case of app with one/few expensive function(s) (e.g. calculating on big datasets) and many light functions (e.g plotting) it seems to work OK.

>

> >
> >

> > > Since it's my first post on this group I would like to start with saying "Hi" to everybody and "Thank you" the dev team for great work on Shiny.

It seems to me that there is some problem with sockjs not being able to talk to browser from node.js child process. Maybe you can help with that.
> > >
> > > Now I am trying to achieve the parallelization from within R - I am using the multicore::parallel function to fork most computationally expensive functions to other process(es) and periodically run multicore::collect from main process to determine if computation is done. So far looks simple and promising, I'll share the results when I finish the implementation.

messages.subject: Re: Chrome/Firefox/Opera gray out
messages.body_plain:
MM2, it has to do with connections where websockets cannot be successfully used. Shiny Server uses SockJS which provides a websocket-like interface that is either implemented using actual websockets if possible, and if not, then it falls back to emulating websockets using older technologies such as XmlHttpRequest.

We tag each SockJS connection with a unique token, this is for security related reasons that are not really worth getting into. If we see a given token more than once, previously we were rejecting the second and subsequent attempts to use the token. But in your cases the token was legitimately getting sent >1 times because the websocket was partially but not fully successful--it succeeded enough to redeem the token but not enough that SockJS considered the connection usable. So the fix I implemented is to allow tokens to be reused.

messages.subject: Re: Why do bootstrap dropdown menus not function inside of Shiny?
messages.subject_clean: Why do bootstrap dropdown menus not function inside of Shiny?
messages.body_plain:
The reason it's not working is probably because of the way that bootstrapPage is defined in your code: you're not replacing shiny::bootstrapPage; instead, you're defining another copy of it in the global environment.

pageWithSidebar is defined in the shiny namespace, so when it calls bootstrapPage, R first searches in the shiny namespace for that function. It finds the function there before it finds your version of the function. So you also need to define your own version of pageWithSidebar -- which have identical code to the shiny version of the function (it will just have a different environment).

You can define the whole pageWithSidebar function, or you can do this to copy the shiny::pageWithSidebar function, and the change its environment:
  pageWithSidebar <- shiny::pageWithSidebar
  environment(pageWithSidebar) <- environment()

-Winston

> Code on Shiny server:  https://gist.github.com/cswarth/6531813

>
> For example, the following is clear
>
> output$nthValue <- renderText({
>   if (input$goButton == 0)

>

>
> fib <- function(n) ifelse(n<3, 1, fib(n-1)+fib(n-2))
>
> shinyServer(function(input, output) {
>   currentFib <- reactive({ fib(as.numeric(input$n)) })
>   isolate({
>   if(actionButton==0)
>   return()

Your question and your code sample seem to point in two different directions. I'll give you solutions for both:

1) A reactive expression that is only calculated upon the press of actionButton (i.e. its value will always be NULL until actionButton is clicked):

currentFib <- reactive({
  if (actionButton == 0)

    return()
  isolate({
    fib(as.numeric(input$n))
  })
})

2) Assigning a non-reactive variable only when a button is pressed:

observe({
  if (actionButton == 0)
    return()
  isolate({
    finalFib <<- reactive({ 1 / fib(as.numeric(input$n)) })
  })
})

Hopefully between those examples there's something that can help you...?

messages.subject: Dynamically Generating Static Web Pages..?
messages.body_plain:
Hello All,

I'm thinking about building a little website where some basic data and jazzy charts are displayed in a standard format, for 100s of different entries in a database. There wouldn't need to be any 'live' analysis. Like building a website long the lines of Wikipedia or IMDB, but with lots of snazzy .js visualisations (thanks to Ramnath!).

I'm keen to use R because of the stats & visualisation capabilities, but mainly because I know R and I'm lazy :)

In terms of how users would place a burden on the server, I get the impression that performance (for fixed cost) would be much better if I could dynamically generate static pages (say once a day, or when new information comes in) which could be stored, served, and connected with managed hyperlinks - as opposed to create a single page app where each user was constantly dynamically generating pages in their own R session. I'm not quite sure what the terminology is for the two approaches.

My hunch is that the sensible answer is "learn Python, and try it's huge web frameworks", but as a dunce R programmer, is there any (even nasty, hacky) way to do this with Shiny? Is this sort of functionality being talked about or planned for the future? Although I haven't read anything about it on the lists, it seems to relate to markdown and Yihui's work (and this post <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/Xavier$20de$20Pedro/shiny-discuss/_WIXv4pk_-4/TAVSFtkhKyQJ>).

If not, if anyone's been successful tackling a similar problem, I'd be keen to know how the approached it!

Apologies for the kind of off topic/ill-formed question,

Brendan

Sorry but Internet Explorer 9 and earlier is not supported if you simply use Shiny from within R. The Shiny package uses websockets to communicate with the browser, and that technology was not introduced in IE until version 10.

If you use Shiny Server then IE 8 and 9 are supported (except for fileInput, which is not implemented for those browsers yet). This is because Shiny Server includes technology that emulates websockets using older technologies that are available in those versions of IE.

messages.body_plain:
TL;DR; For now avoid dots in input/output names as jQuery doesn't like it.

jQuery is the ubiqutious Javascript. It is used by Shiny to find elements in the webpage.

To see an example of what I mean just
run the 09 example runExample("09_upload")  is Chrome, and
press Ctrl + Shift + J to bring up the JavaScript console.
 Now type in $("#file1") then you should see the below
[
<input id=​"file1" type=​"file" accept=​"text/​csv,text/​comma-separated-values,text/​plain" class=​"shiny-bound-input">​
]

This code means to find in the HTML an element where the id = "file1" (basically anything after the "#" is the id). A . (dot) inside $ means to look for something with class = "whatever came after the dot".

So I believe Shiny is trying to run some code like $("#data.file") in Javascript. If you type  $("#data.file") into JavaScript console it should just return null. That's because $ is looking for an HTML element looking like this <... id = "data" class = "file" .... >.

I think the Shiny team just need to escape the . (dot) when they see a dot in the input/output component name as in this stackoverflow question

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/350292/how-do-i-get-jquery-to-select-elements-with-a-period-in-their-id

Now if you type in $("data\\.file") then you should see the correct element returned. Unfortunately I believe this is a bug in Shiny for now.

messages.subject: Emptying read-only variables
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

First of all greetings to all of the developers and users of such an awesome tool! My name is Carlos and I am designing a dynamic browser for a database. I'm still learning how to use shiny so I apologize beforehand if I ask something too obvious. My main question is if there is a way to empty a read-only variable (generated via input) or to clear all of the variables in a session given a trigger (for example deleting a letter from a textInput box). I'll try to explain why I want to do that in the following lines.

The application has a text box where an user inputs its query. Next the application searches for matches to that query, if an exact match is identified a table with results is presented. If no exact matches are found all non-exact matches are presented using a dynamic selectInput generated by renderUI. After the user selects one desired match, the table with results is presented. The problem is that when the user tries to perform another search (without refreshing the browser) the variable containing the output of the dynamic selectInput still contains a value which is presented, regardless of the text in the textInput box. I find it impossible to empty that variable or store it in another place given that my variables are reactive and linked. That is the reason I am looking for a way to empty the read-only variable containing the selected selectInput (or all of the variables in a session given that the user starts erasing text from the textInput box).

Thank you in advance for the help!

Carlos

messages.subject: Re: Why do bootstrap dropdown menus not function inside of Shiny?
messages.subject_clean: Why do bootstrap dropdown menus not function inside of Shiny?
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Winston, before I saw your message I stumbled across reassignInPackage() in R.utils.   That seem to do the trick for replacing bootstrapPage which takes care of pageWithSidebar and friends.

## call with explicit package name to avoid pollution the namespace if we don't have to.
R.utils::reassignInPackage("bootstrapPage", pkgName="shiny", mybootstrapPage)

BTW, the bug in bootstrap V2.1.0 that prevents dropdown menus from clearing is actually fixed in the very next point release, V2.1.1.   I don't know the specific change that fixed it (85 changed files, IIRC) but that seems to be enough to fix dropdown menus.  I'm still advancing to V2.3.2 because it seems to work with shiny and maybe I'll get some other fixes as well.

So now I have dropdown button menus working in Shiny -- sort of - I'll post another question that is specific to the inputBinding problems I am seeing.

On Saturday, September 14, 2013 3:24:04 PM UTC-7, Winston Chang wrote:
> The reason it's not working is probably because of the way that bootstrapPage is defined in your code: you're not replacing shiny::bootstrapPage; instead, you're defining another copy of it in the global environment.
>
> pageWithSidebar is defined in the shiny namespace, so when it calls bootstrapPage, R first searches in the shiny namespace for that function. It finds the function there before it finds your version of the function. So you also need to define your own version of pageWithSidebar -- which have identical code to the shiny version of the function (it will just have a different environment).
>
> You can define the whole pageWithSidebar function, or you can do this to copy the shiny::pageWithSidebar function, and the change its environment:
>   pageWithSidebar <- shiny::pageWithSidebar
>   environment(pageWithSidebar) <- environment()
>
>
> -Winston
>
>
messages.body_snippet:
Thanks Winston, before I saw your message I stumbled across reassignInPackage() in R.utils.   That seem to do the trick for replacing bootstrapPage which takes care of pageWithSidebar and friends.

messages.subject: Re: input text not updated
messages.body_plain:
I believe it's to do with Shiny's default behaviour. For all components and reactives Shiny caches the values being computed. If the computation output produces the same output as cached then it does not do anything further.

In this specific case each time the button is pressed the output$data_set outputs the same HTML so Shiny does not do anything further with it. Whereas if you set the id to some random number then the HTML looks different hence Shiny will go ahead and perform the action. A hacky way to force shiny to output it would be to randomise some part of the HTML as you have done.

I wonder if there is a non-hacky way to do this.

Out of curiosity why does having variable number of inputs prevent you from you using updateTextInput?

messages.subject: Re: Any thoughts on implementing menus in shiny?
messages.subject_clean: Any thoughts on implementing menus in shiny?
messages.body_plain:
Thank you for that pointer - Vincent's app has lots of little gems that I am learning from.   He has efficiently solved the problem I was asking about earlier by explicitly clearing menus in the click callback.  No need to update to a later version of bootstrap.  (I'll update the earlier thread <https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shiny-discuss/_vWyhcZTRhU/nyq_dVUJzNIJ> with this info.)

However he has not solved the problem I am asking about in this thread.   The dropdown menus on his navbar do a single notification and then do nothing if you select the same item again - the same way every control except actionButton works.   That is fine for a navbar but is not what you want for a dropdown menu that should trigger an action each time an item is selected.

However his inputBinding code is much cleaner than what I was doing so I'll incorporate that.  Then I'll just add an integer to values sent back through Shiny from the menu, just like actionButton does, and strip it off in the reactive function.

messages.subject_clean: How to freeze header and left columns of a table output
messages.body_plain:
Possible with some dancing with CSS styles. You can override default bootstrap styles with yours by adding tags$style(type = 'text/css', 'insert your tags here') to ui.r or by creating a separate css file and linking it with tags$link(rel="stylesheet", type="text/css", href=*yourfile.css in www folder")

You may want to check for CSS styles here <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/13378663/html-css-frozen-table-column-on-the-right-side> and here <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/8423768/freeze-the-top-row-for-an-html-table-only>.

I may put up an example on weekend if you kindly remind me.

messages.subject: Re: multiple input with same html element name
messages.subject_clean: multiple input with same html element name
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I don't have a solution yet but there are a few things I noticed.

I see that you have used the name = in your example. My interpretation of the Shiny tutorial (see getId(el) section of http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#building-inputs) is that Shiny looks for id = "some_name" or inputId = "some_name" and then input$some_name can be accessed.

Actually if you have multiple components with the same id then all the component will display in the webbrowser then it might cause "erratic" behaviour. Shiny uses JavaScript to find elements in the HTML when you have two tags/components with the same Id the default behaviour is that it will return the first one only. So for example if you 10 inputs with the same id then it may read the value in the first one only. The Id in html is meant to be unique even though the browser will not force you to do that.

I think you wanted to have an array of inputs. In that cases each id needs to be unique so that you have param1, param2 ...paramn etc. But since the number is variable so n is determined dynamically. I can think of a way to wrap input arrays into a shiny component, let's call that inputArrayComponent. But that requires some javascript so I might wip an example later.

Also I believe [[]] is actually interpreted as a function in R, meaning input$param[[]] actually means apply the "[[" function to input$param, so behind the scene R is trying to run some code like "[["(input$param), if I am not wrong. Maybe can define '[[' to your advantage though.

reactive(...) actually returns a function. You have defined SportPerf as a data.frame initially, but SportPerf <- reactive(...) will overwrite SportPerf as function. So I think the below is closer to what you want.

It's a good idea to replace the SportPerf <- parts of your program to the below. Hopefully this makes sense. Then SportPerf_sex_filter() is passed to ggplot.

  SportPerf_sports_filter <- reactive({

    SportPerf[SportPerf$Sport.1 %in% input$sport, ]
  })

    SportPerf1 <- SportPerf_sports_filter()
    SportPerf1[SportPerf1$Sex %in% input$sex, ]

  output$GPAplot <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(SportPerf_sex_filter(), aes(x=Year, y=Recalculated.GPA))+

      geom_violin()+
      stat_summary(fun.y=median, geom="point")+
      scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,4))+

messages.subject: Re: Using shinyGridster with selectInput
messages.body_plain:
Not really a full blown solution, but a workaround -- the gridster js API exports two functions, .enable / .disable, that can be used to dynamically turn gridster functionality off and on. One can use that to temporarily disable gridster while trying to access a multi-select menu. http://gridster.net/#enable_method for documentation.

One could be clever and disable/re-enable gridster on mouseover for those elements.

-Kevin

messages.subject: File upload (fileInput) privacy
messages.body_plain:
I'm curious to understand a little more about how Shiny handles file uploads.  I'm working on an app that parses some log files from a course management system to help teachers understand more about student interactions in an online learning environment.  Because this involves student data, I want to make sure I consider privacy concerns, and understand what happens to files if a teacher decides to upload their student log data file into a hosted Shiny app.

Currently, all I've been able to learn from the tutorials and package documentation is that fileInput lets you upload data that is stored as "a temp file" and that "this file may be deleted if the user performs another upload operation".
What happens to files when they're uploaded? What directory do they end up in on the server?
When a user uploads a different file during the same session, does it always overwrite the previous file?  Or is it just a possibility that the previous file will get deleted from the temp directory?
It sounds like the file handling is somehow session-based.  When a user closes their browser after uploading and manipulating a file in a Shiny app, what happens to the file on the server?  It doesn't look like the file persists from session to session; when I close out my browser and re-open the Shiny App, it always seems to start fresh with no file.  But is there a possibility that a teacher could upload a log file, close out of their browser, and somehow still have that uploaded file re-appear in a new session on their own or another person's computer?

I'm considering this might actually be better as a non-hosted "pass the code along and run it locally" kind of app, but I'd still love to hear more about file uploads in Shiny!

Alison

messages.subject: Re: File upload (fileInput) privacy
messages.body_plain:
Once uploaded the input$file1$datapath is the path of the uploaded data (assuming file1 is the id of your file upload component).

I tested this out by running it on my Windows XP machine using localhost. It looks like
it created a temporary folder within the temp folder of your current session of R. When R closes the temp folder is deleted.
When I upload another file Shiny created another temporary folder, which is different to the previous one and stores the files there. Again if R closes both of these temporary folders will be deleted.
So I think the overwrite is just a possibility (at least on Windows XP)
Without looking into the Shiny code I suspect Shiny is using the tempdir() function in R to create the temporary folders. The tempdir is probably based on some hashing function so a clash in the output folder name is extremely unlikely as the R guys would have designed the hashing properly
Every new session will start off with the fileInput component being empty. In sounds like you don't want the file to re-appear across different sessions? Especially for another user. If that's your concern I think it should be OK
If you do want the file to persist, there's a way. Running locally I have achieved it by simplifying running the file.rename function of R to copy the file to a folder I know exists. If you have multiple users this approach might not be appropriate though. If your app is hosted on the server and you have no permission to copy files then I have a workaround in that I read the file into R and saved it to the folder I want from R. If I am not write you have write-access to the folder that contains server.R and ui.R

messages.body_plain:
>From memory and a very quick perusal of the code <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/fileupload.R#L90>, I believe ZJ is correct on all counts. A couple of clarifications:
Each file upload operation does create a new subdirectory of the tempdir() folder, with the subdirectory name being 12 randomly generated (runif) hex-encoded bytes. Since it's in the tempdir() folder, other users who can log in directly to the same machine may be able to read these files.
The "this file may be deleted if the user performs another upload operation" is not true today, but I believe it used to be true in the past and could easily be true again in the future (as I prefer that behavior). You should act as if it's true, by copying files you need persisted to a new location.
It's not a great idea to use file.rename to move uploaded files to a new location, because 1) the reactive programming model makes it easy to have your code that does the file.rename called twice with the same temp file path, and 2) file.rename doesn't work when the source and destination paths are on different storage volumes/disks.
Uploaded files are not currently deleted when their session ends, but I would prefer that behavior. We just didn't implement it (yet). Instead, as ZJ says, they are deleted when the R process exits.

messages.subject: Just doublechecking about effect of newly re/created widgets on their observers.
messages.subject_clean: Just doublechecking about effect of newly re/created widgets on their observers.
messages.body_plain:
Motivation: sometimes my app needs to programmatically modify previous user input to keep it consistent with subsequent user input (e.g. if a variable has been selected as the response, it should not remain available as an explanatory variable, that kind of thing).

For transparency/reproduceability/troubleshooting I keep a running log of what the user does and it is important to distinguish what the user directly chooses versus what changes were made by my app in response to user choices.

After some trial and error, I found every time widgets are rewritten as e.g.

    CHANGEFOO<-T;
    output$FOO<-renderUI(if(CHANGEFOO) selectInput('FOOVAR',
                                     'Choose one or more:',
                                     c('A','B','C'),selected=BAR);

...the following seems to happen:

*  Immediately trigger `observe(input$FOOVAR,...)` exactly as if the user manually made the selection equivalent to the value of `BAR` even though no selection has been made.
*  However, if the reloaded `output$FOO` has values selected that are identical to the values before the reload, `observe(input$FOOVAR,...)` will _not_ be triggered.

I just want to make sure that these are both the intended behavior and that I can count on it remaining in future shiny releases?

Because if so, it means I can reliably distinguish what the user did from what the app did by setting a flag in a `reactiveValues` object from inside the `renderUI` call, and have the observer check for that flag. If it finds the flag, it unsets it and emits a log message about the app altering the variables. If it fails to find the flag it emits a log message about the user manually altering the variables.

messages.subject: Re: Javascript and Shiny integration
messages.body_plain:
Yeah, as far as I understand, you can change priorities of observers, but not outputs like renderTable.
What are you trying to achieve? If you just want to change cell background colors, use includeCSS('tables.css') where table.css containing something like #mytable td{background-color: #CCC}
You can also:
- Send raw data to your js through sendCustomMessage and generate table in javascript. You'll have to destroy table in a given div and place a new one with each data update.
or
- Generate table tags in R and pass them to renderText() like I've done here <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/selectable/shiny-discuss/ZaYYmFLHA6U/-cL62wQp0HUJ>.

messages.body_plain:
Julin,

I suspect your problem with runGist is caused by an out-of-date or missing SSL certificate for github.com <http://github.com> on your machine.
You can confirm this by observing the output of this command,

> > shiny:::download("https://gist.github.com/3239667/download", "temp")
> --2013-09-21 14:07:44--  https://gist.github.com/3239667/download
> Resolving gist.github.com... 192.30.252.142
> Connecting to gist.github.com <http://gist.github.com>|192.30.252.142|:443... connected.
> ERROR: cannot verify gist.github.com <http://gist.github.com>'s certificate, issued by `/C=US/O=DigiCert Inc/OU=www.digicert.com/CN=DigiCert <http://www.digicert.com/CN=DigiCert> High Assurance CA-3':
>   Unable to locally verify the issuer's authority.
> To connect to gist.github.com <http://gist.github.com> insecurely, use `--no-check-certificate'.
> Unable to establish SSL connection.

> Warning message:
> In download.file(url, method = method, ...) :
>   download had nonzero exit status
>

If you get an error message similar to the one above you can fix this a couple of ways -- You could go get a current ssl certificate for github (I don't know how to do that),  or you can tell the download tool to no check the certificate.   On my MacOS system I do that with the following command:

> > options("download.file.extra" = "--no-check-certificate")

That's it.   If you want this to be a permanent change in your R environment you will want to put this command in your .rprofile file.

As I am learning more about Javascript I see that this AngularJS framework from Google seems to be getting a lot of buzz and appears to be really popular. In particular I like this concepting of data binding in AngularJS where you can bind a variable in JavaScript to a {{string}} in the HTML/DOM I think it would be nice if Shiny can implement such a feature. It would look something like this index.html ...

There are {{vars} variables to choose from

server.R foo <- reactivevalues(some.var.in.r = 10) output$vars <- bind(foo$some.var.in.R) Now every time foo$some.var.in.R get changesd the HTML/DOM also changes by replacing {{var}} with whatever was assigned to foo$some.var.in.R I believe this can already be achieved with the current Shiny constructs. But I thought providing the bind abstraction actually lessens the amount code needed to achieve this and is much easier to understand. Thoughts?

I believe those are Shiny's intended behaviour. It's to do with Shiny's caching of outputs. If the outputs are the same as before then subsequent process are not triggered.

On Saturday, September 21, 2013 5:16:26 AM UTC+8, Alex Bokov wrote:
> Motivation: sometimes my app needs to programmatically modify previous user input to keep it consistent with subsequent user input (e.g. if a variable has been selected as the response, it should not remain available as an explanatory variable, that kind of thing).
>
> For transparency/reproduceability/troubleshooting I keep a running log of what the user does and it is important to distinguish what the user directly chooses versus what changes were made by my app in response to user choices.
>
> After some trial and error, I found every time widgets are rewritten as e.g.
>
>     CHANGEFOO<-T;
>     output$FOO<-renderUI(if(CHANGEFOO) selectInput('FOOVAR',
>                                      'Choose one or more:',
>                                      c('A','B','C'),selected=BAR);
>
> ...the following seems to happen:
>
> *  Immediately trigger `observe(input$FOOVAR,...)` exactly as if the user manually made the selection equivalent to the value of `BAR` even though no selection has been made.
> *  However, if the reloaded `output$FOO` has values selected that are identical to the values before the reload, `observe(input$FOOVAR,...)` will _not_ be triggered.
>
> I just want to make sure that these are both the intended behavior and that I can count on it remaining in future shiny releases?
>
> Because if so, it means I can reliably distinguish what the user did from what the app did by setting a flag in a `reactiveValues` object from inside the `renderUI` call, and have the observer check for that flag. If it finds the flag, it unsets it and emits a log message about the app altering the variables. If it fails to find the flag it emits a log message about the user manually altering the variables.

David

I think I have run across a bad bug in the new hoverId and clickId functionality for plotOutput() introduced in v0.7.0.
Can anyone else confirm?   Anyone know of a workaround?

The documentation for plotOutput says, "The value will be NULL if the user is not hovering, and a named list or vector with x and y elements indicating the mouse position in user units."
As far as I can tell, that is true only for the first plot you make.   All subsequent hover or click events are reported in the user coordinates of that first plot!
The system never resets the coordinate system.

Live demo: http://spark.rstudio.com/cswarth/testhover

Source code: https://gist.github.com/cswarth/6678546

Run locally:   shiny::runGist("https://gist.github.com/cswarth/6678546")

- chris

messages.subject: Re: Event to close session.
messages.body_plain:
There is actually direct support in Shiny for this (though I can't seem to find documentation for it...):

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  session$onSessionEnded(function() {
    # The session ended
  })
})

There is also a session$isClosed() method.

messages.subject: Re: how exactly are files read into Shiny??
messages.subject_clean: how exactly are files read into Shiny??
messages.body_plain:
inFile is a dataframe, in this case you want inFile$datapath although the extension and name will not be what you expect (it's just a tempfile). If you need it to be with the original filename, you'll need to copy or rename it.

>From ?fileInput:

Whenever a file upload completes, the corresponding input variable is set to a dataframe. This dataframe contains one row for each selected file, and the following columns:
name

The filename provided by the web browser. This is not the path to read to get at the actual data that was uploaded (see datapath column).
size

The size of the uploaded data, in bytes.
type

The MIME type reported by the browser (for example, text/plain), or empty string if the browser didn't know.
datapath

The path to a temp file that contains the data that was uploaded. This file may be deleted if the user performs another upload operation.

messages.subject_clean: Passing dataframe to another tab on Action Button Click
messages.body_plain:
x1, varColCountry, and valColSegment should all be reactive expressions, not variables that are written in an observer. In a reactive expression you can still use the actionButton/isolate pattern in the same way, to defer calculation until after click (you'll just have these reactive expressions return NULL if the actionButton value is 0, and check for NULL wherever these expressions are used).

messages.subject: Re: actionButton, equivalent of "onClick"
messages.body_plain:
For once, side effects are needed! With the code below, the dataset() reactive will return either NULL (on startup), the example dataset, or the uploaded file.

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  values <- reactiveValues(mode = 'none')

  observe({
    if (input$myActionButton > 0) {
      values$mode <- 'example'
    }
  })

  observe({
    if (!is.null(input$file1)) {
      values$mode <- 'file'
    }
  })

  dataset <- reactive({
    switch(values$mode,
      none = NULL,
      example = exampleDataset,
      file = {
        read.csv(input$file1$datapath) # ... and whatnot
      }
    )
  })
})

messages.subject: Suggestions on debugging hosted apps.
messages.body_plain:
Hi. I have an app that runs on 8100 on my local machine, but when I upload it to spark, it freezes (one specific menu grays out and the apps stops responding). I got it narrowed down to a specific line that sets a value in a reactiveValues object. Unfortunately, this flag is what triggers the rendering of most of the other menus.

The appropriate file in my ~/ShinyApps/log/ directory show a normal launch followed by a termination (that would be me typing killall R). When I set options(shiny.trace=T), I get the expected spools of output, but still nothing incriminating.

What should I try next to get to the bottom of this? Ordinarily I would keep put in "cat(...)" statements, dump environments to scratch files and read them from a separate session, and keep poking around until I eventually found it. But the lag will make this a much more lengthy and painfull process than on a local machine. I'm hoping someone can save me some time with suggestions on where to look. Or if perhaps there is somehow a way to get into "browser()" even on a hosted app? Or some way to force it to emit an error message instead of failing silently or (more likely, given the grayed-out behavior of the affected widget) getting into some endless loop somewhere?

By the way, there are no warning or error messages when the same code executes on my local machine.

Or, has there been a change between 0.7.X and 0.4.X that specifically affects setting a value inside a reactiveValues object (from within a renderUI command block, if that matters)? My localhost runs 0.4.1.99 and spark runs 0.7.0.

Thanks.
