server.r

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

masterglmmlm.test <- read.csv("masterglmmlm.q.csv", stringsAsFactors=F)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
 output$textout<-renderText({input$GLMMLM})

  output$main_plot <- renderPlot({
    #get subset of data based on selection
    plot.temp <- reactive({
    gl1<-input$GLMMLM
   df1<-input$df
   model1<-input$model1
   #gl1<-c("MLM","K-EMMA")

    masterglmmlm.test[masterglmmlm.test$GLMMLM %in% gl1 & masterglmmlm.test$model %in% model1 & masterglmmlm.test$df %in% df1,,drop=FALSE]

  })

    p<-ggplot(aes(pos, -log10(p), colour=interaction(GLMMLM, model)), data=plot.temp())+geom_point(aes(shape=df))+facet_wrap(~Locus)

    print(p)
  })

})

messages.subject: Re: Suggestions on debugging hosted apps.
messages.body_plain:
Thank you. I upgraded to 0.7.0 and was able to replicate the problem locally. I apologize for what in hindsight was a lazy question, despite my disclaimers.

It appears that what's different in 0.7.0 is that now writing to a value inside a reactiveValues object causes an endless loop if it's done in a scope that is invalidated by a _different_ value inside the same reactiveValues object. In other words, in 0.4.x it was okay to have a statement like "revals$foo <- 1" in the same enclosure as "bar <- revals$bar" but in 0.7.0 an endless loop results (and it's silent even with "options(shiny.trace=T)", you have to manually cat some sort of message from inside the function in order to see what's wrong).

This can be fixed by wrapping the assignment statement in "isolate()".

Another side note about upgrading shiny that might matter to someone:

I'm running R 2.15.3 on Lucid 10.04.4 LTS. When I tried to "install.packages('shiny')" it failed on compiling the "httpuv" package. When I did "devtools::install_github('httpuv'); devtools::install_github('shiny')" it worked but claimed to install v0.6.0.99. However, when I again tried "install.packages('shiny')", it installed v0.7.0 with no further comments.

messages.body_plain:
I do not think performance is the primary reason. eval(parse()) just
looks so bad and unnecessary. What input$foo does is to turn the
symbol foo into a character string "foo", and extract the element
named "foo" in input. Then it is just so straightforward to make the
character name in the very beginning and use input[["foo"]] directly.

The $ method also has a few limitations, due to the R syntax
requirement, e.g. normally you cannot have spaces in the symbol name,
so you cannot do input$foo bar (have to input$`foo bar`), or you
cannot do input$in since 'in' is a reserved keyword. Weird things like
this can happen, but [[]] will always work, e.g. input[["foo bar"]],
input[["in"]], ... Note this is not specific to Shiny. It is a general
issue in R.

In other cases, eval(parse()) is often an indication of the awkward
design of the program. Normally you do not have to write code that
generates code. That said, I myself use eval(parse()) a lot for other
purposes :)

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>

messages.body_plain:
Java doesn't run well on Spark and Glimmer. This is because we lock down processes to 2GB of virtual memory using "ulimit -v" (in response to a few users repeatedly consuming dozens of GB of RAM, whether on purpose or accidentally). By default, Java attempts to reserve lots and lots of virtual memory (without actually allocating it) so it crashes.

http://superuser.com/questions/472587/why-does-limiting-my-virtual-memory-to-512mb-with-ulimit-v-crash-the-jvm

Try calling this BEFORE using any rJava functions, to tell Java to limit the heap to 512MB:
.jinit(parameters="-Xmx512m")

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server Error
messages.body_plain:
Configurable timeouts are a feature of the master branch now. However, the instructions for building and installing Shiny Server have not been updated since we did widespread refactoring this summer. The next release of Shiny Server will bundle its own copy of Node.js and be installed using a .deb or .rpm. We don't have a date yet for when this release will be, but it's high on our priority list.

messages.subject: Population ecology with shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone

Just thought I'd post something to let you know I've been developing some interactive population modelling apps with shiny. Don't have a gist set up for them at the moment but if anyone wants the code just ask - they're mostly using deSolve to give solutions for the differential equations. I'll be using these as part of my population ecology course that I teach and I hope they'll make it easier for me to convince a bunch of biology students that mathematical modelling can be useful.

These are the ones that are ready for prime-time so far, more to follow.

http://87.117.69.131:3838/Logistic/

http://87.117.69.131:3838/Lotka_Volterra_Competition/

http://87.117.69.131:3838/Hutchinson_delay_logistic/

http://87.117.69.131:3838/JMS_discrete_logistic/

Cheers

Rob K

messages.subject: How to embed the Jmol applet into a Shiny Application?
messages.subject_clean: How to embed the Jmol applet into a Shiny Application?
messages.body_plain:
Dear users,
I'd like to visualize molecular models into a Rshiny application, coordinate files like XYZ or PDB. The easiest way is to use the applet Jmol (an open-source Java viewer for chemical structures in 3D, http://jmol.sourceforge.net/index.en.html) but the question is how to embed such a tool into an Rshiny application in an easy way (I'm an R user but not expert in HTML or java)?

All ideas, documents, suggestions and comments will be welcome!

All the best and congratulations for Rshiny!

Josep M. Campanera,

messages.subject: Extracting data from a table and displaying few rows of it using RODBC and shiny
messages.subject_clean: Extracting data from a table and displaying few rows of it using RODBC and shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hi shiny users,

Thanks in advance.

I am using R-3.0.1 and shiny on Windows XP.

May I request you to assist me for the following please.

I've gone through the e-mail archive but could not get a definitive answer.

I have attached the codes. While running, I receive the following error:

> runExample("webstats")

Error in source(serverR, local = new.env(parent = .GlobalEnv)) :

K:/R-3.0.1/library/shiny/examples/webstats/server.R:1:2: unexpected input

1: {\

^

>

I can access the data outside shiny. But my intention is to access data from a table (user can select a table) within shiny to make a dynamic presentation.

Once again, thank you very much for the time you have given.

Regards,

Deb

ui.R

-----

library("shiny")
library("RODBC")

ch<-odbcConnect("DSN",uid="uid",pwd="pwd")
tables <- sqlTables(ch)

tables <- tables[tables$TABLE_TYPE == "TABLE", ]
odbcClose(ch)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

headerPanel("Test for RODBC"),

sidebarPanel(
selectInput("Table", "Choose a table:",
choices = tables$TABLE_NAME),
numericInput("Records", "Number of Records to view:", 25)
),

mainPanel(
tableOutput("view")
)
))

server.R

-----------

library("shiny")

library("RODBC")

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

output$view <- reactiveTable(function() {

ch <- odbcConnect(("DSN",uid="uid",pwd="pwd")

schema_table <- paste(input$Table, sep="")

result <- sqlQuery(ch, "select * from POPULATION")

odbcClose(ch)

head(result, n= input$Records)

})
})

messages.body_plain:
Doable with CSS and JavaScript. Tab headers are links and can be selected with <a> tag. Try adding
tags$style(type = "text/css", "a{color: #f50000;}")
to your ui.R to paint tab text in red.
This would change all links in your app to red. To avoid that, use "li a{color: #f50000;}" instead

a:visited pseudo selector wouldn't work on tab links, so you'll probably have to resort to JavaScript to highlight visited tabs.

messages.subject: Re: CSS tag list for shiny UI-elements
messages.subject_clean: CSS tag list for shiny UI-elements
messages.body_plain:
The recipe I suggested works. Say you want to size file input and it's progress bar.

First the Browse button and a file name.
Pick this element in Firebug. It corresponds to the <input id="fileInp" class="shiny-bound-input" type="file">

You can change it by id (fileInp is how I called it in R) and write #fileInp{width:100%;}. "#" means id selection in CSS. In that case only this file input will resize.

If you want to change multiple elements at once you need do select a group. You can navigate to style tab in firebug and notice that it is set to auto in bootstrap.min.css input[type="file"]{width:auto;}
auto means it would fit its content. So if your filename is long, your control would be to wide and will go outside the sidebar. So we need to either set it to fixed px/em or in % of parent width.
Therefore, add input[type="file"]{width:100%;} to your styles to override the whole group, or input{width:100%;} to change all inputs.

Now the progress bar.
By default its width is set inline to 100% and the bar is located inside
<div id="fileInp_progress" class="progress progress-striped shiny-file-input-progress" style="visibility: visible;">
So you can either select it by id like #fileInp_progress:{width:80px;} to change individually, or by class with a (.progress) selector:
.progress{width:80px}

That's the easiest way to do it. If you want extra work, all the class names can be found in bootstrap.min.css and shiny.css, try to figure them out :)

Am Freitag, 27. September 2013 12:06:15 UTC+2 schrieb Kirill Savin:
> The recipe I suggested works. Say you want to size file input and it's progress bar.
>
> First the Browse button and a file name.
> Pick this element in Firebug. It corresponds to the <input id="fileInp" class="shiny-bound-input" type="file">
>
> You can change it by id (fileInp is how I called it in R) and write #fileInp{width:100%;}. "#" means id selection in CSS. In that case only this file input will resize.
>
> If you want to change multiple elements at once you need do select a group. You can navigate to style tab in firebug and notice that it is set to auto in bootstrap.min.css input[type="file"]{width:auto;}
> auto means it would fit its content. So if your filename is long, your control would be to wide and will go outside the sidebar. So we need to either set it to fixed px/em or in % of parent width.
> Therefore, add input[type="file"]{width:100%;} to your styles to override the whole group, or input{width:100%;} to change all inputs.
>
> Now the progress bar.
> By default its width is set inline to 100% and the bar is located inside
> <div id="fileInp_progress" class="progress progress-striped shiny-file-input-progress" style="visibility: visible;">
> So you can either select it by id like #fileInp_progress:{width:80px;} to change individually, or by class with a (.progress) selector:
> .progress{width:80px}
>
> That's the easiest way to do it. If you want extra work, all the class names can be found in bootstrap.min.css and shiny.css, try to figure them out :)

Indeed, when I add

                tags$style(type = "text/css", "a{color: #f50000;}")

```

De : Kirill Savin <kirill...@gmail.com>
À : shiny-...@googlegroups.com
Envoyé le : Vendredi 27 septembre 2013 4h02
Objet : Re: controlling title color in tabPanel()

Doable with CSS and JavaScript. Tab headers are links and can be selected with <a> tag. Try adding
tags$style(type = "text/css", "a{color: #f50000;}")
to your ui.R to paint tab text in red.
This would change all links in your app to red. To avoid that, use "li a{color: #f50000;}" instead

a:visited pseudo selector wouldn't work on tab links, so you'll probably have to resort to JavaScript to highlight visited tabs.

messages.body_plain:
Never use eval(parse(input$a)) in a Shiny app, or anything that looks like that.

The reason is not elegance, it's security. What happens if the (malicious) user decides to set input$a to system("rm -rf ~/")?

The only time it is remotely OK to use eval(parse()) in Shiny is if you can guarantee that the value you're evaluating could not possibly have come from user input (that includes from a database whose values came from the user).

messages.body_plain:
The shinyIncubator package has a progress indicator that is designed for this purpose. Install it from GitHub like so:

if (!require("devtools"))
  install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("shiny-incubator", "rstudio")

In your ui.R, add library(shinyIncubator) at the top and progressInit() somewhere else in your UI (i.e. in mainPanel). It doesn't matter where you place progressInit, the progress widget is always pinned to the upper right of the screen.

For server.R, see ?withProgress for details.

messages.subject: Re: Error with updateSelectInput
messages.body_plain:
It is in reference of updateSelectInput. See example section.
?updateSelectInput

The basic idea is that every reactive variable inside observe() is monitored for changes and when the change happens, the expression inside observe() re-runs. In your case the variable is input$obs.
Reactive outputs such as renderPlot/renderTable/renderUI/renderText act in the same manner, but updaters do not, so you need to wrap them in observe().

Reactivity overview <http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity-overview> is a nice start, but it is not exhaustive.

messages.subject: Re: Using uiOutput to show a long loading state. Is it possible?
messages.subject_clean: Using uiOutput to show a long loading state. Is it possible?
messages.body_plain:
There are several problems here. If you don't use loadedResult anywhere, it won't execute; reactive expressions are lazily evaluated. And your usage of observe here is unnecessary; observe is used to execute and automatically re-execute a chunk of code whenever its reactive dependencies change. In this case, you're only assigning, so there are actually no reactive dependencies at all, so the observer code will just execute once and no more:

loadedResult <- reactive({
  if( input$loadButton > 0) {

    observe( rv$loadIndictaor <- "loading")

    temp <- loadFunction(object)

    observe( rv$loadIndicator <- NULL )

    return(temp)
  }
})

This would be closer (but still won't work for reasons I describe below) (I put the NULL assignment inside on.exit so it is called even if an error occurs in loadFunction):

observe({
  if( input$loadButton > 0) {
    rv$loadIndictaor <- "loading"
    on.exit(rv$loadIndicator <- NULL)
    temp <- loadFunction(object)
    return(temp)
  }
})

The reason this doesn't help is because Shiny waits until all outputs are done computing and then pushes all the new values to the browser at once. We found that this was more intuitive behavior than updating the outputs one at a time. You can, however, send messages to the client without waiting for all the output to be ready, if you know JavaScript; see https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-incubator/blob/master/R/progress.R#L127 and https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-incubator/blob/master/inst/progress/progress.js#L35 for an example.

messages.subject_clean: Extracting data from a table and displaying few rows of it using RODBC and shiny
messages.body_plain:
Kirill,

Thanks for your response.

1. shiny version

Package: shiny

Type: Package

Version: 0.1.0
2. webstats

webstats is a subdirectory and like this: \R-3.0.1\library\shiny\examples\webstats

I have saved ui.R and server.R in this directory.

To run this, I type runExample("webstats") at the R command prompt.

3. reactiveTable is deprecated. Try changing it to output$view <- renderTable({
I've done that.

4. I have provided the new ui.R and server.R

ui.R

-----

library("shiny")

library("RODBC")

ch <- odbcConnect("******", uid= "******", pwd= "******")

odbcQuery(ch,"SELECT table_name")

tables<-sqlGetResults(ch)

odbcClose(ch)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

headerPanel("Test for RODBC"),

sidebarPanel(

selectInput("Table", "Choose a table:",

choices = tables$TABLE_NAME),

numericInput("Records", "Number of Records to view:", 25)

),

mainPanel(

tableOutput("view")

)

))

server.R

-----------

library("shiny")

library("RODBC")

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

output$view <- renderTable(function() {

ch <- odbcConnect("******", uid= "******", pwd= "******")

schema_table <- paste(input$Table, sep="")

result <- sqlQuery(ch, "select * from POPULATION")

odbcClose(ch)

head(result, n= input$Records)

})

})

5. Where as outside shiny (it works well):

library(RODBC)

channel <- odbcConnect("******", uid="******", pwd= "******")

sqlTables(channel) # I get names of the tables

odbcClose(channel)

Once again, thank you very much for the time you have given.

Regards,

Deb

messages.subject: Persistent sessions
messages.body_plain:
I tried posting this in the thread called 'Persistent R sessions" (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/persistent/shiny-discuss/g5FbYp5Iyj8/WLb-UDtAxgsJ) but it got deleted.

I have shiny 0.7.0 running on an Ubuntu 12.04.2 LTS machine. When I launch an app using Chrome browser, three processes get created. However, when I close the browser window, the three processes persist. The processes don't end until I manually kill them using sudo killall R. Because of this issue a few apps that use Sys.Date() to popualte dateInput() are not refreshing the date. For example, if I clear all processes using the killall command and launch the app today, it will show today's date (9/30/2013) correctly. Now if I close the browser and launch it again tomorrow, it will show 9/30/2013 instead of tomorrow's date (10/1). If I then kill the processes, it will show tomorrow's date correctly.

The discussion in the "Persistent R session" thread was about this problem occurring in Ubuntu 13.04. Does anyone know why this might be happening in 12.04.2 LTS?

Thanks!

messages.subject: Feature request for emailing apps
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

My team at the company I work for would find it very useful to have emails periodically delivered to our inboxes that shows a given app at its current state. We're basically looking for a snapshot of the app currently running on Shiny server and have it sent to our inboxes, perhaps on a fixed schedule.

Is there any option to do that at the moment, or is that a feature that can be considered for the enterprise version?

Thank you!

Alan

output$myChart <- renderMap({
